title: Low-degree finite-module Kummer cohomology of the two geometric lines
statement: Let Ω be algebraically closed, A a finite commutative ring, ell a prime invertible in Ω, N≥1 and ell^N A=0. On X=A1_Ω and U=D(t), let F=mu_(ell^N) tensor A with the canonical coefficient map. H1(U,F) is A-linearly isomorphic to A, carrying the actual Kummer class of t to 1. H1(X,F)=0. No freeness of A over Z/ell^N is assumed.

source.place: Steps 1--3; unit proof paragraphs Coefficients and Degrees 0 and 1; Milne Sections 14 and 16.

proof.text: Transport the free rank-one R=ULift(Z/ell^N) computation on polynomial and Laurent spectra to the actual affine line and coordinate open, using the canonical scheme isomorphisms, open cohomology equivalence and normalized Ext/evaluation comparison. These preserve the Kummer extension and coefficient insertion. Thus H1 of the affine line with coefficient R is zero and tau_R:R→H1(U,R(1)), a↦a*kappa(t), is an isomorphism.

For either line object let G(M)=H1(mu_(ell^N) tensor the constant R-module M). The proved kummerModuleTwist_preservesFiniteColimits applies directly to the actual coefficient twist. The proved rightDerived_preservesFiniteColimits_of_succ_isZero, with H2 vanishing for every coefficient sheaf from finite_line_high_cohomology, shows that H1 on R-module sheaves preserves finite colimits. Consequently G preserves finite colimits. The coefficient insertion tau_M(a) is additive and natural by its pure-tensor formula. The proved coefficient-generator theorem works directly with the natural transformation from underlying additive groups to G, so no extra linear structure on the cohomology functor is required for the finite-presentation step.

Apply the proved kummer_coefficient_generator_bijective to the actual Kummer class on the punctured line, with the rank-one computation and finite-colimit preservation from steps 1 and 2. This includes the insertion maps, their additivity and naturality, and the finite free presentation argument. For affine-line H1, apply the finite-module criterion to the transformation from the zero functor, whose rank-one component is invertible by vanishing.

Use the underlying R-module of A. The explicit scalar-extension/tensor comparison identifies its twist with the abelian sheaf underlying the actual finite Tate line, and preserves the coefficient insertion x tensor a. Naturality of tau for multiplication by a in A proves A-linearity after the module/abelian derived-evaluation comparison. Its inverse sends the actual coordinate Kummer class to one. The affine-line computation gives its H1 vanishing.

theorem finite_line_low_cohomology (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    (ℓ N : ℕ) (hℓ : ℓ.Prime) (hℓΩ : IsUnit (ℓ : Ω)) (hN : 1 ≤ N)
    (hA : ((ℓ ^ N : ℕ) : A) = 0)
    (hm : IsUnit ((ℓ ^ N : ℕ) : Γ(Line (Spec (CommRingCat.of Ω)), ⊤))) :
    let S := Spec (CommRingCat.of Ω)
    let X := Line S
    let F := Scheme.finiteEtaleTateSheaf A (ℓ ^ N) X hA 1
    let H := ((sections X.smallEtaleTopology A (openObject S)).rightDerived 1).obj F
    ∃ e : H ≅ ModuleCat.of A A,
      e.hom (kummerClass A X (openObject S) F (ℓ ^ N) hm
        (Etale.ordinaryFiniteRootMap A (ℓ ^ N) hA X) (coordinateUnit S)) = 1 ∧
      IsZero (((sections X.smallEtaleTopology A
        (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X))).rightDerived 1).obj F)
